brief.headline: The three reports split: one sees strength, one sees worry, one sees little change.
brief.consensus_summary: Three sources reported. They do not form a collective directional view: one is bullish, one is bearish, and one is neutral.

conflicts.why_it_matters: Smart money against the crowd, the classic informative divergence.
conflicts.in_plain_terms: They disagree on whether steady buying from larger investors matters more than the current cautious mood among shorter-term traders.
conflicts.description: Market-intel points to net ETF inflows of $295 million over four sessions and exchange reserves down by 9,800 BTC as evidence of bullish accumulation. Sentiment-analyst points to the Fear & Greed Index at 31 in Fear, down from 52, a long/short ratio of 0.81, and eight-hour funding at -0.009% as evidence of bearish positioning. The market-intel view is set over weeks, while the sentiment-analyst view is set over days.
conflicts.case_for_a: For market-intel to be right, the ETF inflows and falling exchange reserves would need to reflect sustained accumulation by buyers with a multi-week horizon, strong enough to absorb the short-term selling pressure implied by the sentiment data.
conflicts.case_for_b: For sentiment-analyst to be right, the Fear & Greed reading of 31, the long/short ratio of 0.81, and negative funding would need to signal enough trader caution or forced selling to overwhelm the buying that shows up in ETF inflows and exchange reserves.
conflicts.what_would_resolve_it: The next daily ETF flow print, showing whether net inflows continue near the $295 million pace or turn negative, would resolve which signal is stronger.

internal_divergences.detail: MACD has just crossed up while the MA stack remains bearish.
